454. Palindromic Number from Concatenation

Problem Statement:
Jack gives you a list of N positive numbers in the form of an array A Jack wants to know if it is possible to construct a palindromic number from the given list A palindromic number is one that reads the same when reversed. For example: 828 is a palindromic number since its reverse has the same value. The number 2134 is not a palindromic number since its reverse 4312 is not equal to 2134. To construct a palindromic number Jack takes any two numbers present in the list A[i] and A[j] and concates them : A[i]+A[j] Report "YES" if it possible to form a palindromic number or "NO" if it is not possible to form a number in the manner given above NOTE: if a palindormic number is already present in the array it does not count as "YES" since we are not following the method above to construct the number.
input_spec: First line contains a single integer N denoting the number of numbers in the list. The second line contains N integers.
output_spec: The output consists of a single line: either :"YES" or "NO" .
